new_task_1.title: Preserve pandas-native index semantics during label lookup
new_task_1.description: xarray 2026.1.0 now wraps array-like lookup labels in `pd.Index` before delegating to pandas `Index.get_indexer`, including the nearest-bound localization path used by interpolation. This keeps pandas-backed indexes operating with their native dtype semantics during lookup instead of relying on raw NumPy/list coercion.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that xarray label-resolution paths preserve pandas index dtype semantics when asking pandas to resolve labels, so pandas-backed indexes continue to work correctly for array-like selection and nearest-bound localization.

expectation.grounded: Internal lookup helpers that call `pandas.Index.get_indexer` should pass a pandas `Index` built from the requested labels rather than a raw NumPy array or Python list. In particular, multi-label index resolution should call `get_indexer(pd.Index(flat_labels), ...)`, and interpolation localization should call `get_indexer(pd.Index([minval, maxval]), method="nearest")` when locating the bounding source region.
expectation.conceptual: When xarray delegates label matching to pandas, it should preserve the lookup values as pandas index objects so pandas can apply its normal dtype-aware matching rules for string, datetime, timedelta, and other pandas-backed index types.

constraints.grounded: This change should only normalize the target passed into pandas lookup routines. Existing selection semantics, `method`/`tolerance` behavior, float16 promotion, result shapes, and error handling for genuinely missing labels should remain unchanged apart from the restored compatibility of dtype-sensitive pandas lookups.
constraints.conceptual: Treat this as a compatibility fix in the lookup boundary between xarray and pandas, not as a redesign of xarray indexing semantics.

behavior: Array-like label lookup paths now convert flattened labels to a pandas `Index` before calling pandas `get_indexer`.
Nearest-bound localization used during interpolation now passes the min/max lookup values as a pandas `Index` rather than a plain list.
Lookup operations against pandas-backed indexes preserve pandas-native dtype handling instead of depending on NumPy/list coercion of the target labels.
Existing lookup options such as `method` and `tolerance` continue to flow through to pandas unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: When a label-based xarray operation resolves multiple labels against a pandas-backed index, it should delegate those labels to pandas as a pandas `Index` and return the same matches pandas resolves under that dtype-aware lookup path.

When interpolation localizes the relevant source slice using nearest matching on a pandas-backed coordinate index, it should compute the boundary positions by calling pandas `get_indexer` with a two-element pandas `Index` containing the computed min and max target coordinates.

When lookup values rely on pandas index dtype semantics rather than plain NumPy coercion, xarray selection and interpolation should complete without changing the established matching rules or the shape of the resulting xarray object.
When labels are truly absent or otherwise invalid, the operation should continue to fail according to the existing indexing rules rather than silently altering missing-label behavior.
